title: Rapid 1:1 prep — Miguel Park & Sofia Martinez (Feb 14 2027)
content:
Purpose: quick, focused sync (20–25m). Align on top outcomes this sprint, unblock any issues, and cover one coaching topic.

Context (quick):
- Sofia is mid-sprint on the cross-batch KV cache stabilization work (feature branch merged to staging Tuesday). Perf regression observed in long-seq benchmarks after quantization patch.
- On-call next week (Tue–Thu) — want to confirm rotation handoff and playbook updates.
- Career: Sofia asked for feedback on backend-to-platform stretch work and interest in small-IC leadership on the cache rollout.

Agenda (20–25 min):
1) 3 min — Quick personal check-in (energy, any non-work blockers)
2) 7 min — Technical sync: KV cache/regression status + immediate mitigations
   - Current: staging perf +12% median latency for sequences >1024 after quantization change (bench: long_seq_v2)
   - Hypothesis: kernel scheduling change + suboptimal batching profile for long sequences.
   - Ask: what experiments blocked? what do you need from me?
3) 5 min — Ops: on-call handoff & playbook gaps (who will carry runbook edits?)
4) 5 min — Career/feedback: review next growth step and small leadership trial (own cache rollout doc + runbook ownership)
5) 2–5 min — Review action items & quick wins

Prep notes for me (manager):
- Bring up tradeoffs: short-term revert vs targeted kernel config (cost/latency implications).
- Offer 2-hour unblock slot this Friday for pairing on benchmarks (offer specifically to run long_seq_v2 profile).
- Confirm whether Sofia needs a peer review buffer for rollout doc before canary. Suggest reviewer: Lina Choi or Ezra Kim.
- Ask about mental load + capacity — is this a good time for a leadership trial? propose 4-week scope.

Signals I care about (metrics to check quickly):
- long_seq_v2 median token-latency: baseline vs staging (target < +5% delta)
- nightly e2e benchmark pass rate (percent of jobs passing): target 100% for core suites
- number of open PR comments blocking merge: ideally 0–2 for canary
- on-call pager volume last 7 days: want < 5 high-severity pages for Sofia's team

Potential prompts/questions to surface during 1:1:
- What was the last experiment you tried to isolate the regression? What did it rule in/out?
- If you could get one thing from me to move this forward in 24h, what would it be?
- How confident are you in the rollout timeline (0–10)? What would move it 2 points?
- Do you want me to pair-review the rollout doc or coordinate reviewer?

Action items (to capture at end):
- Sofia: run targeted kernel switch test (A/B) against long_seq_v2 and paste results in the Jira ticket (ENG-4821) — due 2027-02-16.
- Miguel (me): reserve 2 hours Fri 09:00–11:00 PT for pairing on benchmarks; send calendar invite — due 2027-02-14 (today).
- Sofia: draft 1-page rollout runbook and assign Lina for review; link in PR description — due 2027-02-18.
- Miguel: update team on on-call rotation + add a short checklist item to runbook for quantization-related incidents — due 2027-02-15.
- Both: quick sync after Sofia's A/B results if regression persists (15 min ad-hoc) — contingent.

Follow-up notes template (we'll paste post-meeting):
- Decisions made: (e.g., revert/no-revert, owners for runbook edits)
- Action owners + due dates (copy from above)
- Any blockers requiring escalation (who to escalate to: e.g., infra-plat lead, release-eng)

Quick personal note to leave the meeting on a positive: thank Sofia for pushing the cache work; call out one specific recent win (reduced cold-start by 18% in canary last week) — helps morale and signals concretely the impact.

Scratch: If regression is due to batching heuristic, then short-term plan: adjust batching threshold for sequences >512 only (low-risk), run canary in dedicated queue to avoid impact to production, monitor token-latency + error rates for 24 hours.

End of doc.
